question: Will everyone see the majesty of God?
summary: Isaiah 40:5 declares that the glory of YHWH will be revealed and all flesh — kol basar — will see it together. Isaiah 26:10, four chapters into the so-called 'Isaiah Apocalypse,' says the wicked will not behold the majesty of YHWH. The two declarations sit fourteen chapters apart in the same book, and the contradiction is internal to Isaiah.

reconcile.connective: Gill answers that "all flesh" see only "with the eyes of ... understanding" — a universal gospel offer the unconverted refuse, not literal sight guaranteed to all.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses exactly this pairing, reading the texts as flatly opposed: universal sight promised, then denied to the wicked.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Will Everyone See God's Majesty?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/majesty.html)

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), p. 181
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this exact pairing verbatim under 'See the Divine glory. Will not see it,' harmonizing: 'The wicked will not voluntarily recognize the "majesty" ... of the Lord; but he will eventually be compelled to see and acknowledge it ... at the last great day.'

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: and all flesh shall see it together; not the Jews only, but Gentiles also; not with their bodily eyes, but with the eyes of their understanding; even the salvation of the Lord, and his glory, as displayed in it, being set forth in the everlasting Gospel to the view of all …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill's gloss on 'all flesh shall see' limits the sight to 'the eyes of ... understanding,' the standard harmonizing move that lets Isa 26:10's unconverted wicked fail to behold while Isa 40:5's universal offer still stands.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed..... Christ himself, who is the brightness of his Father's glory, and his own glory, as the glory of the of the only begotten of the Father; the glorious perfections of his nature, seen in the miracles wrought, and in the doctrines taught by him; the glory of the divine Father, in the face or person of Christ; and the glory of his attributes, in the work of salvation by him; all which is most clearly discerned in the glass of the Gospel, or in the ministry of the word, by John, Christ himself, and his apostles:
and all flesh shall see it together; not the Jews only, but Gentiles also; not with their bodily eyes, but with the eyes of their understanding; even the salvation of the Lord, and his glory, as displayed in it, being set forth in the everlasting Gospel to the view of all; see Luk 3:7,
for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it: that his glory should be revealed, and be visible to all, and therefore sure and certain; for what he has said he does, and what he has spoken he makes good. The Targum is,
"for by the word of the Lord it is so decreed;''
and therefore shall be fulfilled.
